404 Media recently reported a loophole in the iCloud+ "Hide My Email" feature that allowed anyone to access a user's real email address. Apple has now said the issue has been officially fixed.

Apple said the security flaw in "Hide My Email" was patched earlier this month

If you're an iCloud+ or Apple One subscriber, Apple's "Hide My Email" privacy feature is particularly useful and can do a great job of protecting your real email address.

Here's how it works, according to Apple's official website:

However, according to a recent report from 404 Media, "Hide My Email" has long contained a loophole that could let anyone uncover the real email address linked to an Apple account. The revelation has also given rise to a new proposed lawsuit.

But Apple said today that the flaw was officially fixed earlier this month.

Apple told 404 Media that it "released a patch for this issue on July 3 and claimed the issue had been completely resolved".

This iCloud+ vulnerability was first reported to Apple by Tyler Murphy in June 2025. After initial communication, Apple claimed to have patched it, but Murphy found the problem was still there. Hopefully this time it has truly been resolved once and for all.

How often do you use the iCloud+ "Hide My Email" feature? Let us know in the comments.
